evidence: Moisture affects self-sustained combustibility and calorific value; increasing moisture decreases calorific value because heat is used to vaporize water. Notes ~7 MJ/wet kg as a common incineration viability threshold.
methodological_use: Justifies giving food/organic and weather moisture indicators positive risk weights.

issue: Risk index: food waste recovery and LHV
evidence: Modelled Lisbon residual MSW and found 100% food waste recovery increased residual LHV by 36.8% due to reduced moisture fraction.
methodological_use: Justifies food/organic waste as the dominant moisture-risk dimension and supports high weight on food/organic share.

evidence: Generalised LHV models use wet physical composition; paper and plastics/combustibles are relevant predictors. The paper notes paper waste contribution to LHV can be high.
methodological_use: Justifies dry combustible indicator such as paper+plastic+wood/textile as a risk-reducing or LHV-supporting dimension.

evidence: LHV prediction equation based on wet physical composition was developed; combustibles, food waste and ash content affect heating value.
methodological_use: Supports use of composition-based LHV scenarios and proxy fuel-quality screening when measured bunker LHV is unavailable.

source: OECD/JRC Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators
evidence: Indicators should be normalised, weighted and aggregated according to an underlying theoretical framework; robustness/sensitivity analysis should test weights, normalisation, imputation and aggregation.
methodological_use: Justifies transparent theory-driven weighting plus sensitivity analysis rather than arbitrary single weights.

evidence: When observations are grouped and errors can be correlated within clusters, failure to control for clustering can produce misleadingly small standard errors and inflated t-statistics.
methodological_use: Justifies clustering Seoul panel standard errors by date because weather regressors are common across districts on a given date.

evidence: Data quality should be assessed as fitness for purpose; key components include completeness, accuracy, integrity, consistency and timeliness.
methodological_use: Justifies replacing note-count scores with a transparent data-confidence rubric.

evidence: Korean WtE plants have design/operational LHV benchmarks and LHV is central to energy recovery efficiency.
methodological_use: Justifies using Korean facility-literature benchmark as a benchmark/case-specific interpretation, not as a directly comparable composition-model value.
